summary: Guidance: idempotency key hashing + salt encoding causing duplicated function/tool calls across Python/TS SDKs
description:
Issue summary:
Customer BrightCart reports duplicate function/tool invocations when client retries cross region. Suspected root cause is inconsistent idempotency-key hashing and 'salt' byte encoding between Python and TypeScript SDKs plus intermediate header normalization at an edge proxy.

Impact:
- Duplicate downstream webhook calls and double-ordered inventory updates for 2 customers (BrightCart staging->prod migration).
- Increased billing for customer by ~2x on a subset of long-running orchestration flows.
- Customer is on Dedicated plan, needs mitigation for live traffic.

Environment:
- Customer uses dedicated capacity in us-east with fallback to eu-west.
- SDKs: python-sdk v1.9.3, ts-sdk v2.1.0 (both pinned in their app).
- Requests use streaming with per-action funcall idempotency header X-Idempotency-Key.

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1) Python client starts stream, sends tool call with header X-Idempotency-Key: bytes->sha256(hex) base64-encoded.
2) Network glitch causes client to retry connection to eu-west fallback.
3) TS service receives replayed request; its SDK computes idempotency token by hashing the UTF-8 string of the original key (no canonicalization of binary salt) and encodes to URL-safe base64.
4) Edge proxy (edge-sidecar) normalizes and splits large headers (http2 chunking) which alters padding characters ('=' removed) and '+' -> '-' substitutions.
5) Server treats keys as different and re-executes tool/function.

Logs / evidence:
- BrightCart supplied paired request IDs showing identical request body but different X-Idempotency-Key values on server logs (us-east vs eu-west).
- SDK traces show python-sdk set header: "X-Idempotency-Key: Q2hlY2tTYWxtMQ==" and ts-sdk shows "X-Idempotency-Key: Q2hlY2tTYWxtMQ" (missing padding).
- Edge logs show header rewrite on 2026-03-12T22:14:08Z with code path edge-sidecar/h2-split.

Customer asks: recommended SDK best practices and immediate mitigations to avoid duplicates while we investigate permanent fix.
comments: 2026-03-13 - Maya Chen (Support): Logged issue after BrightCart reported duplicate webhook side-effects. Provided initial request/response pairs to SRE team.
2026-03-13 - BrightCart (customer@brightcart.com): We see double inventory debits in orders placed between 22:12-22:18 UTC. We can pause the workflow but need guidance before cutover tomorrow.

2026-03-13 - Ethan Cole (Support): Asking customer for SDK versions, exact X-Idempotency-Key values, and edge proxy vendor; requested sample curl replay test and consent to run a canary with idempotency-canonicalization header set.

2026-03-14 - SRE (Liam Patel): Confirmed edge-sidecar performs header normalization during http2 header chunk reassembly. Noted that removal of '=' padding in some proxies is observed; forwarded to SDK owners for canonicalization plan.

2026-03-14 - SDK-TS Owner (Priya Nair): Reproduced missing padding when using URL-safe base64 encoder without explicit padding option. Drafting patch to normalize to standard base64 with explicit '=' padding prior to sending.

2026-03-14 - SDK-PY Owner (Diego Alvarez): Python uses raw bytes -> sha256 -> base64.standard_b64encode which preserves padding. Noted inconsistency. Will add canonicalization API to normalize to urlsafe with explicit padding or canonical header transform.
2026-03-14 - Ethan Cole (Support): Shared short-term mitigations to customer (below). Customer acknowledged and will apply canary tonight.
investigation_notes: Edge-sidecar http2 header chunking shown to strip trailing '=' padding characters in some configurations (observed on vendor version 3.2.1).
Python SDK currently emits standard base64 with '=' padding; TS SDK defaulted to urlsafe base64 without padding in v2.1.0.
Idempotency keys sometimes include binary 'salt' bytes appended by orchestration layer which must be canonicalized to a stable serialized form across languages.
Race condition: when retry routes cross region, different SDK normalization leads to divergent keys; server lookup is string-based and therefore misses deduplication cache entry.
Attempted local replay tests with a small harness: reproduces duplicate tool invocation when header padding differs or '+' vs '-' substitutions occur.
Related to prior tickets involving header truncation and padding (linked SUP-761001 and SUP-472999).
short_term_workaround:
Advise customer to enable SDK-level canonicalization option or to layer a deterministic hex-encoded idempotency token. Steps:
1) In Python: change idempotency key generation to use hex digest of sha256 (sha256(...).hexdigest()) and set header X-Idempotency-Key to hex string.
2) In TS: temporary patch to convert incoming idempotency token to lower-case hex via crypto.createHash('sha256').update(...).digest('hex').
3) If hex change is not possible, configure edge proxy to preserve header padding and disable url-safe normalization.
These mitigations avoid base64 padding/network normalization differences.
long_term_fix_plan:
Planned multi-step fix: 
- SDKs: introduce explicit IdempotencyKey.canonicalize() utility in python-sdk and ts-sdk that emits lowercase hex or canonical padded base64 with header-safe escaping. Target patch releases: python-sdk v1.9.4, ts-sdk v2.1.1.
- Server: accept and normalize both padded base64 and hex formats for idempotency lookup for a transition period (6 weeks).
- Edge: add guidance and an automated check in our deployment validator to ensure proxies preserve header padding for critical headers.
Owners: SDK teams + Serving runtime. Estimated ETA: 2026-03-28 for SDK patches, 2026-04-10 for server backwards-compat support.
resolution: Workaround provided and applied by customer: switched to hex-encoded idempotency tokens for the affected workflow. No duplicate invocations observed during a 12h canary window. SDK teams opened PRs to add canonicalization helper and tests. Post-deployment monitoring alerts created to watch for duplicate funcall counts. Follow-ups: ensure server accepts dual formats and update public SDK docs with canonical idempotency recommendations.
postmortem_followup_items: SDKs: land canonicalize helper and add cross-language interop tests (owners: Priya Nair, Diego Alvarez)
Serving runtime: add tolerant idempotency-key parser and migration window (owner: SRE - Liam Patel)
Docs: update 'idempotency and retries' guide with recommended hex-canonical token and examples for Python/TS/Go (owner: Docs - Nora White)
Support: proactively reach out to enterprises on dedicated/private to recommend canonicalization (owner: CS - Maya Chen)
